about.title: Cudahy Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and it's common to feel unsure of what to do next while still grieving. Cudahy sits in a densely populated stretch of Los Angeles County, and while the most recent full-year data shows no recorded traffic deaths, the city still logged 34 injury collisions along corridors such as Atlantic Avenue, Clara Street, Wilcox Avenue, and Santa Ana Street — a reminder that serious harm can happen quickly on these streets. If a loved one has died because of someone else's negligence, California law gives certain family members a path to pursue accountability through a civil wrongful death claim, separate from anything happening in criminal court. Our team handles wrongful death claims and can review the circumstances, explain your standing under California law, and walk you through what comes next without added pressure during an already difficult time.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people — typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. We can clarify where your family fits before any decisions are made.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Window
items.desc: California law generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity involve a much shorter deadline. Reaching out early helps preserve your family's options.

items.title: Losses That Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: Recoverable losses in a wrongful death case can include funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the non-economic loss of love, companionship, and guidance. We can help you understand which losses may apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Cudahy?
items.answer: Under California law, families generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If the claim involves a government entity or public roadway maintained by a city or county agency, the deadline to act is much shorter. Speaking with us soon after a loss helps make sure nothing is missed.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring this kind of claim?
items.answer: California law prioritizes a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children as the first in line to file. If none of those relatives exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the circumstances. We can review your family's situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: Cudahy's crash data shows no recorded traffic deaths in the most recent year — does that mean wrongful death claims still happen here?
items.answer: Yes. Public crash counts reflect a single reporting year and can shift, and injury collisions — 34 of them recently, with 51 people injured — show that serious harm along corridors like Atlantic Avenue and Wilcox Avenue is still a real possibility. Wrongful death claims can also arise from incidents beyond traffic collisions, so it's worth having a conversation regardless of the yearly statistics.

items.question: Does this service charge anything to help us?
items.answer: No. We provide free help at no cost, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover compensation for your family. Contact us directly to have an attorney guide the legal process.
